data.reasoning: The only valid vote (deepseek) correctly identified the package as a standard, safe Rust PKGBUILD with pinned checksums and no malicious top-level code or build-time injections. The 'inconclusive' result from qwen was due to a transient API error (HTTP 400) on .SRCINFO, which carries no verdict signal. The advisory report from openrouter corroborates the safety. There are no .install hooks or other maintainer files to review.
data.disagreement_analysis: The initial trigger was 'disagreement (inconclusive safe)', but the inconclusive verdict was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in the qwen model, not a genuine security disagreement. The deepseek model provided a clear, valid 'safe' verdict with sound reasoning.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit .SRCINFO due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in an inconclusive package verdict.
learnings: Distinguish between tool errors (e.g., API timeouts or 400 errors) and genuine security inconclusiveness when triggering escalation audits. A tool failure should not be treated as a security disagreement.
Implement retry logic for transient API errors during file audits to prevent a single file failure from cascading into an inconclusive package verdict.
